newsitem.title: FINLAND: KONECRANES CEO SEES FASTER 97 SALES GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: KONECRANES CEO SEES FASTER 97 SALES GROWTH.

text.p: Finnish cranes maker KCI Konecranes International Oy said on Wednesday expected net sales growth in 1997 to be stronger than the 12.3 percent increase in 1996 over the previous year.
"The growth is likely to be a bit stronger this year than last year," Konecranes CEO Stig Gustavson told a news conference.
Konecranes earlier released its preliminary 1996 report, which showed a 2.45 billion markka turnover, up from 2.18 billion in 1995.

Konecranes' 1997 net sales would be boosted by growth in all three business areas -- standard lifting, special cranes and maintenance services -- and also by German company MAN GHH Logistics', which Konecranes acquired in November, he said.
But Gustavson said the group's margins would not necessarily rise in proportion with net sales.

"Don't make the mistake of just extrapolating our 1996 margins into 1997," he said, adding that the rapid growth could "take a certain toll on margins" particularly in the maintenance services business area.
Konecranes' 1996 profit after financial items was 208 million markka, up from 135 million in 1995.
